issues.legal_issue: A landlord seeking possession for immediate demolition and reconstruction need not prove that the premises are in a condition requiring immediate demolition, and a more profitable use after reconstruction may support the landlord’s requirement.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction to demolish the existing building and erect a new one, saying the premises were old and unsuitable for continued occupation.
The landlord had obtained municipal sanction, had made preparations for reconstruction, and had sufficient means to carry it out.
The courts found the landlord’s requirement reasonable and bona fide, and considered the prospect of a better return after reconstruction.
An engineer said the building, although old, could continue to exist for about 15 more years.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s requirement under section 21(1)(j) concerned the landlord’s reasonable and bona fide need for immediate demolition and reconstruction, not the physical condition of the building. Proof that the building required immediate demolition was unnecessary, and the prospect of more profitable use after reconstruction could be considered in the landlord’s favour.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 21(1)(j) of the Mysore Rent Control Act, 1961, the landlord must establish a reasonable and bona fide requirement for the immediate purpose of demolishing the premises and erecting a new building. That requirement is assessed in light of surrounding circumstances, including the landlord’s means and steps taken for reconstruction; a more profitable use after reconstruction may also be considered. Section 21(1)(k)’s specific reference to the condition of the building supports not importing that requirement into clause (j). Neta Ram v. Jiwan Lal was relied on for treating the possibility of more profitable use after construction as a relevant circumstance. The contrary interpretation in Mehsin Bhai v. Hale & Company was disapproved. Sections 26(1), 27 and 28(1) provide tenant protections connected with commencement of demolition, occupation of the new building, and notice of its completion.

predicates.demolition_reconstruction_eviction_case: The proceeding seeks recovery of possession so the landlord can demolish the premises and erect a new building.
predicates.landlord_has_reasonable_bona_fide_need: The landlord’s need for the premises for the proposed redevelopment is reasonable and bona fide in light of the surrounding circumstances.
predicates.landlord_seeks_immediate_demolition_for_: The landlord seeks possession for the immediate purpose of demolition followed by construction of a new building.
predicates.structural_necessity_need_not_be_proven: The landlord need not establish that the premises’ physical condition makes immediate demolition necessary.

issues.definition: When a landlord brings a redevelopment eviction proceeding and has a reasonable, bona fide need for immediate demolition and rebuilding, structural necessity need not be proven.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s claim for compensation for improvements does not arise for consideration in the eviction proceeding.
material_facts: The tenant claimed that the value of improvements made to the premises should be paid before eviction was ordered.
The Rent Controller found that the claim, even if established, did not prevent the landlord from obtaining possession.
The Supreme Court stated that the compensation claim did not arise for consideration in these proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The tenant’s claim for compensation for improvements was not for consideration in the eviction proceeding.
issues.legal_principle: The Court stated that the claim did not arise for consideration in the eviction proceedings; it cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this point and did not decide any independent entitlement to compensation.

predicates.eviction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a landlord’s application to recover possession from a tenant.
predicates.tenant_claims_compensation_for_improveme: The tenant asks to be paid for improvements made to the premises before eviction.

issues.definition: When a tenant claims compensation for improvements in an eviction proceeding, that claim is not considered as part of that proceeding.
